contentHtml:
清华大学国际合作与交流处和清华大学材料学院将于2026年8月5日联合举办清华大学授予约翰·彭德里（Sir John Pendry）名誉教授仪式暨海外名师讲堂。本次活动特邀帝国理工学院理论固态物理学讲席教授约翰·彭德里，就“超材料：从负折射和隐身到时空晶体”作专题演讲。诚邀广大师生参与。

内容简介：

过去数年里，人类已经能够制备具备全新电磁特性的材料，由此催生了一个全新的研究领域。这类材料被称作超材料，性能突破了传统材料的固有局限，能够产生自然界中不存在的奇特物理效应，负折射效应便是其中之一。

受这些全新研究前景的启发，理论科学家依托这类新材料提出了诸多突破性构想：我们如今可以研制出一种透镜，其成像分辨率不再受自然法则制约，唯一的限制只在于工艺能否达到设计标准；我们可以操控电磁波的传播路径，绕过障碍物，实现物体隐身；我们还能够研发出在可见光频段具备磁响应特性的人工材料。

讲座的最后，我将介绍时空晶体这一前沿方向：在时间和空间维度上构筑材料。时空晶体打破了时间反演对称性，为新型器件的研发开辟了道路。理论物理学家对其抱有浓厚兴趣，借助它，人们有望在实验室中实现霍金辐射。

该领域至今涌现出不计其数的创新成果，而未来还有更多突破有待发掘。超材料正发展为一项颠覆性技术，包括一系列需要精准调控光场（或是更为广义的电磁辐射）的应用场景，涵盖5G与6G通信、卫星通讯、太阳能采集、隐身技术、生物成像传感以及高性能核磁共振设备等众多领域。

主讲人简介：

约翰·彭德里教授是伦敦帝国理工学院的理论固态物理学讲席教授。他于1969年获得剑桥大学博士学位，1972年至1973年在贝尔实验室工作。自1981年起，他在伦敦帝国理工学院布莱克特实验室担任教授。彭德里教授是诸多学术团体的会士，包括英国皇家学会、美国国家科学院、美国艺术与科学院等。2004年，他因对科学的贡献被授予英国荣誉爵士称号。他因在表面结构及其与电子和光子相互作用的开创性研究而享誉全球。他创立了“超材料”领域，发现负折射材料可以用来制备完美透镜，规避了困扰科学界一个多世纪的阿贝衍射极限。他提出的转换光学为设计任意调控电磁场的超材料提供了理论模型。

演讲时间： 2026年8月5日（星期三）14:30 17:00（14:00入场完毕）

演讲地点： 清华大学主楼接待厅

演讲语言： 英文

主办单位： 清华大学国际合作与交流处、清华大学材料学院

扫描下方二维码完成在线报名。清华大学校内师生请当天携带个人学生证（工作证）入场；校外人员建议绿色出行，请携带身份证入校。

Join the Ceremony for the Conferment of Tsinghua University Honorary Professorship on Sir John Brian Pendry on ‌August‌ 5 organized by the Office of International Affairs and the School of Materials Science and Engineering, this special event features a lecture by Sir John Pendry, Chair in Theoretical Solid State Physics at Imperial College London.

内容简介：

In the last few years a new area of research has emerged as a result of our ability to produce materials with entirely novel electromagnetic properties. Known as metamaterials because they take us beyond the properties of conventional materials, they display remarkable effects not found in nature, such as negative refraction.

Spurred on by these new opportunities, theorists have produced exotic concepts that exploit the new materials: we can now specify how to make a lens whose resolution is limited not by the laws of nature but only by our ability to build to the stated specifications; we can guide radiation along a trajectory, avoiding objects and causing them to appear invisible; we can design and manufacture materials that are active magnetically in the optical range.

I shall conclude my lecture discussing the latest developments which aim to structure materials in time as well as space - space/time crystals. These materials violate time reversal symmetry and offer possibilities for new devices. Theorists find them intriguing as they offer possibilities for creating Hawking radiation in the laboratory.

There has been a truly amazing amount of innovation but more is yet to come. The field of metamaterials is developing into a highly disruptive technology for a plethora of applications where control over light (or more generally electromagnetic radiation) is crucial, amongst them 5G/6G technology, satellite communications, solar energy harvesting, stealth, biological imaging and sensing, and enhanced MRI scanners.

Professor Sir John Pendry is the Chair in Theoretical Solid State at Physics Imperial College, London. He received his Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge in 1969 and worked at Bell Labs from 1972-1973. He has held his professorship in the Blackett Laboratory (Imperial College, London) since 1981. Prof Pendry is a Fellow of many academic societies, including the Royal Society, the National Academy of Sciences of United States, American Academy of Arts and Sciences, etc. In 2004, he was knighted in the British Honours for his services to science. Professor Pendry is recognized worldwide for his pioneering work on the structure of surfaces and their interaction with electrons and photons. He founded the field of “metamaterials”, a concept for engineered structures whose electromagnetic properties depend on their internal structure rather than their chemical constitution. He discovered that a perfect lens manufactured from negatively refracting material would circumvent Abbeʼs diffraction limit to spatial resolution, which has stood for more than a century. His most recent innovation of transformation optics gives the metamaterial specifications required to rearrange electromagnetic field configurations at will.

Time: Wednesday, ‌August‌ 5, 2026, 14:30 17:00（No entry after 14:00）

Venue: Reception Hall, Main Building, Tsinghua University

Language: English

Organizers: Office of International Affairs, Tsinghua University

‌School of Materials Science and Engineering, Tsinghua University

Scan the QR code below to complete the online registration. Tsinghua University faculty and students are required to bring their student ID/ faculty ID for entry on the day of the event. We recommend that external attendees use green transportation and bring their ID card when entering the campus.
